result.title: E5-CEILING (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1): pre-registered T-0 predictability ceiling for the +30%/5-session event from daily bars, with a directional (up-minus-down) ranker as the kill test
result.thesis: Null (what I expect): there is no long edge in daily-bar public-price signals after costs because the +30%-in-5-sessions event is a variance event in a fat-tailed cross-section, not a directional one. Daily-bar features can identify names whose variance is about to be high (the only pre-event separator ever found is 20-session volatility, matched-set AUC 0.68 IDX / 0.78 US / 0.56 crypto, E1/E2 REPORTs), but variance is symmetric and high-variance names carry flat-to-negative drift, so every detector built from bars inherits a non-directional lift: P(+30%) rises together with P(-23%) and the mean 5-session return stays at or below matched controls. The recorded evidence is consistent with this and not with a cost story: in every recorded trading run the GROSS mean is already negative (IDX 20261008T000401Z gross -3.67% vs net -4.06%; crypto 005732Z gross -1.51% vs net -1.90%; US 060443Z gross -3.19% vs net -3.65%; US 115656Z fill B gross -0.10% vs net -0.97%), i.e. the cost drag is 0.4-0.9pp of a 1-4pp loss. The decisive and cheapest test is therefore not another plan search but a ceiling: give a frozen, pre-registered learner the entire daily-bar information set (the E1/E2 weak-signal lists already pre-registered as E1-SIGNALS-v1 / E2-SIGNALS-v1), fit it once on discovery over the whole evaluable universe (not conditioned on any frozen detector), freeze the coefficients as literals in a rule module, and trade its top 0.5% of ticker-days under the original harness plan against matched controls. Arm A (E30 ranker) tests the detection-to-profit link the program assumed; Arm B (directional ranker: logit P(up 30%) minus logit P(down 23%)) tests whether ANY daily-bar feature combination at T-0 carries tradeable direction. The mechanism that would make the thesis true is that some combination of features (e.g. quiet price with creeping volume, drawdown plus rising range, breakout in a low-vol name) separates the coming up-moves from the coming down-moves; the mechanism that would make the null true is that every such combination predicts both tails equally.
result.why_not_already_falsified: (1) Signal family: E1 (F1..F10) and E2 (G1..G11) are hand-written one- or two-threshold rules; all admissible members are inside-the-move by construction (ret1>=30%, ARA lock, 5-session +30%). No experiment ever combined features, ranked the cross-section, or used the one pre-event separator (vol20) as an input (G11_HIGHVOL_ACTIVE was admissible in E2, US 9.7x, and never selected or traded). (2) Information source: the weak-signal AUCs (E1/discovery/signal_stats.csv, E2 REPORT.md line 38) were univariate, discovery-only, and computed against controls matched on price_band/liquidity/market_cap only (idxsig/e1.py Study._pool, keys line 220), never turned into a detector. (3) Structure: E3 (108 plans) and E4 (144+288 short plans) searched execution, not information; US_BREAKOUT_v1 is a single feature; E3_US_RETENTION_v1 is a one-feature filter on G2 flags. None measured the DOWN-event rate of any detector's flags, so 'variance detector vs direction detector' is untested. (4) The gross-vs-net decomposition above (from recorded trades.csv.gz gross_return/net_return columns) shows the failures are gross, so repair_v3's cost-bound rerun and further fill-model work cannot change signs; the remaining degree of freedom is the information set, which E5 exhausts for daily bars. (5) The oracle/break-even bound has never been written down: E1 validation gives capturable_median 0.0% for F1_ARA flags, but no run has computed E[net | E30] and E[net | not E30] under the plan to state the precision a detector would need to break even against matched controls.

protocol.family: MOONSHOT_E5 (idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py, new): per market two pre-registered logistic rankers over the full evaluable universe. Features (all from the 12 RULE_FIELDS, causal, per-session cross-sectional percentile ranks plus their squares; NaN rank -> 0.5): ret1, rel1, ret5, ret20, volr, valr, rngr, cpos, vol20, dd60, up5, zero20, age, logval20, brk60; plus gap (US/CRYPTO only) and ara (IDX only). Definitions verbatim from research/E1/protocol.json weak_signals (E1-SIGNALS-v1) / research/E2/protocol.json (E2-SIGNALS-v1); freqr, turn, logmcap excluded (not live-computable from Yahoo fields). Labels on the reference chain (e1.Study.level, HORIZON 5): U = max close t+1..t+5 >= 1.30 x close t (= E30); D = min close t+1..t+5 <= close t / 1.30. Learner: L2 logistic regression, lambda fixed in protocol.json (1e-3 x n), IRLS 25 iterations in numpy, all positives plus a 10% seeded negative subsample weighted 10 (seed 20261015), one fit per (market, label). Arm A score = logit_U; Arm B score = logit_U - logit_D. Threshold: the discovery-period 99.5th percentile of each arm's score (top 0.5% of evaluable ticker-days, comparable to F1_ARA's 0.54% flag rate in 2023); fixed, never searched. Coefficients and thresholds are committed as module-level literal tuples (audit.py allows literals) so the rule hash covers them.
detectors: ORACLE_E30 (diagnostic bound only: signal = the E30 truth matrix, executed via execution.execute + controls.matched_draws, never a rule, never recorded via write_run)
protocol.plans: One plan only, the original harness model so results are comparable to E1/E2 and no plan search is added: IDX entry at the next close (entry_lag 1), US/CRYPTO entry at the next open, fixed exit at the 5th close, overlap skip, no stop. Primary fill model A (ex-post 10% of entry-session volume, as the pinned E1/E2 runs); pre-registered sensitivity runs under fill C (IDX, registry) and fill B (US as_traded on panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z; CRYPTO) whose sign must agree before any policy consequence.
markets: IDX (TIER_1, panel pinned to the E3 manifest panel-20261013T194245Z rebuilt from manifests, registry ca_registry-20261013T194256Z)
US (panel_us-20261008T004105Z for fitting/validation A; panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z for the fill-B sensitivity; survivor-only, stated)
protocol.discovery_period: IDX 2021-01-22..2022-12-30; US and CRYPTO 2020-07-01..2022-12-31 (fit, threshold, in-sample admissibility; labels need t+5 inside the period, as e1.Study.elig)
protocol.validation_period: 2023 only (IDX 2023-01-02..2023-12-29; US/CRYPTO 2023-01-01..2023-12-31), one recorded harness run per admissible arm; --end is set explicitly for US/CRYPTO because HEAD has no code-level GLOBAL_HOLDOUT (backtest.py:251-252); IDX is guarded by backtest.HOLDOUT. 2023 is a once-seen year for the frozen detectors' flags; E5 is designed without it and any pass is provisional until prospective paper outcomes agree.
protocol.admissibility: Stage 1 (discovery, in-sample, per arm): report AUC_U, AUC_D, flags, E30 and D30 precision and lift vs matched random (e1.Study.evaluate pattern extended with a D30 block), directional ratio lift_up/lift_down with 1000-resample bootstrap CI, and the harness trading run with matched controls. An arm is admissible for validation only if, on discovery: scored >= 200, avg net > 0, one-sided p < 0.05 vs matched random (200 draws, floor 0.005), avg net > 0 in every discovery year with >= 50 scored (e3.admissibility reused verbatim). An arm that fails IN-SAMPLE is dead without a validation run (cheapest kill). Stage 2 (validation, one run per admissible arm, recorded via write_run): pass iff scored >= 100 (US >= 200), avg net > 0, avg net > matched mean, one-sided p < 0.05 vs matched, and the sensitivity fill model does not flip the sign of (rule minus matched). Primary endpoint = Arm B per market; Arm A, the D30 diagnostic, the ret1<10% (pre-move) vs >=10% split, gross vs net, capturable median, and the ORACLE bound (E[net|E30], E[net|not E30] under the plan and the implied break-even precision p* = (matched - E[net|not E30]) / (E[net|E30] - E[net|not E30])) are reported, not judged. Multiplicity: 3 primary tests, each declared; the thesis-level verdict is 'daily-bar T-0 information absent' iff 0/3 Arm B pass.
protocol.matched_controls: Harness controls v2 (idxsig/controls.py VERSIONS['v2']: price_band, liquidity, market_cap [IDX mirror era], volatility, momentum, drawdown, listing_age; 200 draws per attempted signal, seed 20261007+1, relaxed from the last feature below MIN_POOL 5), executed under the identical ExecConfig, plus the same-session uniform baseline; exactly as backtest.run does for every recorded run. Detection metrics use e1.Study's 3-feature pool for comparability with E1/E2 result.json. Because the controls match volatility tercile, a ranker that merely picks high-vol names is compared against high-vol names: that is the point.
protocol.costs_model: Profile defaults unchanged (idxsig/profiles.py): IDX fees 0.15% buy / 0.25% sell, lot 100, notional Rp10,000,000; US per-side price-tier cost 1.5%/0.5%/0.15%/0.05% plus SEC fee, notional $5,000; CRYPTO 0.1% fee + 0.1% slippage per side + 0.1% tier, notional 5,000 USDT; max_participation 0.10; no price impact, no dividends. Gross and net both reported from trades.csv.gz.

data_needed: IDX panel-v2 rebuilt from data/manifests/panel-20261013T194245Z.json (the csv is not on disk; build-panel from the pinned mirror commit bc0ac771) and ca_registry-20261013T194256Z.csv (on disk); fallback for a dry run: panel-20261007T225823Z.csv.gz is on disk
US panel_us-20261008T004105Z.csv.gz (on disk) and panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z.csv.gz (on disk, for fill B as_traded sensitivity)
No new external data, no network, no holdout rows (all windows end 2023-12-29/31)
code_changes: research/E5/protocol.json + PROTOCOL.md (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1): frozen and committed before any statistic, sha256 stamped into every stage output (e3._stamp pattern); fields: feature list and definitions, rank transform, learner (lambda, iterations, subsample seed), threshold quantile 0.995, labels U/D, periods, harness blocks per market, selection = none (no model search), admissibility (e3.admissibility), validation pass rule, consequence_if_passed/failed, claims

idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py (new, passes idxsig.rules.audit: imports numpy/pandas only, module-level literals only, no I/O): RULE_ID 'MOONSHOT_E5_<MARKET>_D1', VERSION 'v1', FEATURE_ARGS ('close','prev','high','low','volume','value','present','tradeable','lock_up','open'); features() = moonshot_g.features copied verbatim plus valr, rngr, up5, zero20, age, logval20, ara computed as in idxsig/e1.py Study._signals (lines 163-188); rank() per session via pandas rank(pct=True); score(f, coef) = dot of ranks and squared ranks with literal COEF_U / COEF_D tuples per market; THRESHOLD literal per (market, arm); candidates E5_CAND_<MARKET>_<ARM> before the freeze, SELECTED tuple per market after it; compute(m) returns 1 where score >= threshold, 0 elsewhere, NaN where not tradeable; causal by construction (prefix-first check in rules.causal_signals)
idxsig/rules/__init__.py registry(): add moonshot_e5 to the module tuple (line 61-64)

idxsig/e5.py (new, modelled on e3.py): protocol(); build_dataset(df, meta, market, period) reusing e1.Study's level/r5max machinery and adding r5min for the D label, elig mask as Study.elig; fit_logistic(X, y, lam, seed) numpy IRLS; run_discovery(): fit both labels, write discovery/model.json (coefficients, thresholds, in-sample AUCs), detection metrics for both arms (Study.evaluate pattern + D30 block + directional ratio + pre-move split), trading runs via backtest.run with signal_cache (e3.run_discovery lines 214-225), admissibility via e3.admissibility, ORACLE bound via execution.execute + controls.matched_draws with the same ExecConfig (labelled bound), summary.json with the freeze instruction 'copy model.json coefficients into moonshot_e5 literals and commit'; run_validation(): refuses unless moonshot_e5 literals equal discovery/model.json, one backtest.run per admissible arm recorded via results.write_run, detection.json, sensitivity run under fill B/C, result.json with passed/consequence (e3.run_validation lines 266-294)
idxsig/cli.py: e5-discovery / e5-validation --market IDX|US|CRYPTO wired like e2-* (cli.py:134, 370-385) and e3-* (dirty-tree refusal, protocol sha); force end <= validation end for US/CRYPTO

tests/test_e5.py: audit passes on moonshot_e5; module literals == research/E5/discovery/model.json; labels U and D symmetric on a synthetic panel; causal_signals raises no LookaheadError; threshold reproduces the protocol quantile; registry lists MOONSHOT_E5_* only after SELECTED is set

No change to backtest.py, execution.py, controls.py, paper.py; the paper ledger is untouched (a paper policy for E5 would be a later, separate POLICY_ID and needs the paper._detector hook, out of scope here)
result.falsifier: The skeptic's null is falsified if, in any market, Arm B (directional ranker, frozen before validation) passes 2023: scored >= 100 (US >= 200), average net > 0, average net above the matched-random mean with one-sided p < 0.05 (200 draws), and the sensitivity fill model (C for IDX, B as_traded for US, B for crypto) keeps rule-minus-matched positive. The moonshot thesis (daily-bar T-0 information is tradeable) is falsified if Arm B fails in-sample admissibility on discovery or fails the 2023 run in all three markets; the sharper reading that detection is variance detection is confirmed if, in addition, Arm A's D30 lift vs matched is within the bootstrap CI of its E30 lift (directional ratio CI covers 1) and the ORACLE break-even precision p* exceeds the highest E30 precision ever recorded for a daily-bar detector (23.55%, F1_ARA discovery).
risks: 2023 is a once-seen validation year: outcomes of the frozen detectors' 2023 flags are known to the researchers, so a pass is pre-registered but not virgin and must be confirmed prospectively (paper ledger) before any policy change; the holdout stays sealed
US panel is survivor-only (flatters longs): a US-only pass is weak evidence; IDX TIER_1 (survivorship-complete) is the decisive market; crypto includes delisted pairs

A rank-logistic with squared terms is a bounded learner: a null means 'no edge findable by this pre-registered learner', not a proof; a second learner would be a new protocol (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v2), not a retune
Fill model A is ex-post optimistic (E2 repair: 224 fills accepted only on final entry-session volume averaged -7.03%); hence the sensitivity requirement under B/C before any consequence
Multiplicity: 3 markets x 2 arms; mitigated by declaring Arm B primary and reporting Arm A; no threshold, lambda or feature search
US 2020-2022 split units are unverified (repair panel read_through 2023-12-29); return-based rank features are unit-free but price_band/logval20 are not; reported, not fixed

Compute: US discovery matrix ~2.7M rows x ~35 columns; the seeded negative subsample keeps the fit under a few GB; the harness trading runs take seconds (IDX) to minutes (US) each, as E3's 108 runs took ~21 min
Crypto delistings and EXIT_DATA_END trades are scored at the last close as in E2; a ranker that favours dying pairs inherits that convention on both rule and control sides
Daily bars cannot prove an opening fill at size and model no intraday path (quality.py:27); the result bounds daily-bar information, not intraday information
result.directive_compliance: Holdout: every window ends 2023-12-29 (IDX) / 2023-12-31 (US, crypto); IDX runs are refused by backtest.HOLDOUT unless --holdout-final, which E5 never passes; US/CRYPTO --end is pinned in protocol.json because HEAD has no code guard (backtest.py:251-252); no holdout row is read, labelled or scored; the holdout remains reserved for one final test after prospective evidence. No retune: E1 F1_ARA, E2 G2_RET30, E3 candidates and E4's plan are not touched; E5 is a new family whose only inputs are the pre-registered E1/E2 weak-signal definitions, fitted on discovery alone with no model, threshold or feature search; validation is one run per arm. No manufactured results: every number comes from backtest.run with 200 matched draws under the identical plan, recorded through write_run into results/runs and RUNS.jsonl (append-only, dirty-tree refusal); the ORACLE arm is labelled a bound and is never recorded as a run or presented as performance; gross-vs-net figures quoted here were read from recorded trades.csv.gz and are historical. Pre-registration: research/E5/protocol.json is committed before any statistic, its sha256 is stamped in every stage file, stage directories are created once (exist_ok=False) under the append-only guard, and the freeze (coefficients as rule-module literals) is committed before validation so the rule hash covers the model. No real orders, no ASTRA change, no paper-policy change: a pass would only justify a later, separate POLICY_ID wired through paper._detector and judged prospectively.
result.expected_information_value: Either way the program learns something it cannot learn from another plan or cost rerun. If Arm B fails in-sample on discovery in all markets (likely, and the cheapest outcome: no validation run needed), the whole daily-bar price-only detection family is closed on information grounds, not execution grounds, and the only remaining places for edge are non-price timing data (EDGAR acceptanceDateTime, Nasdaq Nordic releaseTime, both reachable in principle per the data map) or intraday order flow, neither of which the repo has; the honest consequence is 'stop the daily-bar moonshot family; do not build more scanners on it'. If Arm A passes detection with high E30 lift but fails trading while its D30 lift is equally high, the mechanism behind E1/E2's 9.3x/5.4x/4.6x 'detection' is nailed down as variance detection, and the ORACLE break-even precision p* gives a closed-form reason why 15-23% precision loses: future proposals can be rejected by arithmetic. If Arm B passes in a market and survives the fill sensitivity, the coefficient vector names which daily-bar features carry direction (the first located edge in the program), and the next step is a prospective paper policy for MOONSHOT_E5_<MARKET>_D1, still without the holdout. The pre-move/inside-move split tells, in every case, whether any remaining lift exists before the first +10% day, which is the only kind a retail participant could act on.
